content:
Lean core recently got an Html type, while the original one from ProofWidgets has been protected, requiring you to write it as ProofWidgets.Html.

@𝚠𝚘𝚓𝚌𝚒𝚎𝚌𝚑 𝚗𝚊𝚠𝚛𝚘𝚌𝚔𝚒, could you maybe say what the difference is and if/when we should switch to using the Html type in Lean core? Will the one in ProofWidgets be deprecated?

The new Lean.Html type represents "actual" HTML, as in the WhatWG spec. It is meant for authoring HTML documents. We are now using it in Verso and doc-gen.

The type ProofWidgets.Html represents HTML-trees-with-Lean-widgets. It is, in retrospect, badly named - it should have been WidgetHtml or something - and is now protected to avoid clashes with Lean.Html. However, I have no immediate plans to rename (to avoid churn) or deprecate it - it serves a different purpose than Lean.Html. Deprecation would happen only if Lean core gets its own widget-HTML type.
